label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Agency native)
explanation: Diagnosis: the unedited model solves competition-math problems correctly early but is trapped in a self-reinforcing "re-verification" loop and never emits </think>/\boxed{}; layer-23 attention copies its own recent lines and adds ~+10 nats to the loop-continuation token while ` réponse`'s logit barely differs from escape states (only a few nats below competitors). A constant pro-` réponse` push would need to be ~residual-sized to win, so instead I built a gated rank-2 LoRA that adds a component along the ` réponse` unembedding direction (row 248069) with magnitude set by a linear gate on each module's true input. The gate direction a = normalize(mean(h_escape) - h_early) (computed from traced unedited activations with the end token controlled to "\n") is positive in reasoning-complete/stuck states and negative at the start of reasoning; a second rank row b = mean-input direction provides an offset, and the two coefficients were solved per module by least squares so the effective ` réponse` push is ~+0.7-1.4 units in loop/escape states and ~0 early. Applied only at late layers (mlp.down_proj of layers 18,20,22,23 and self_attn.o_proj of layer 23), so early/mid computation is untouched. Estimated effect: about +21 nats of ` réponse` logit in loop states and +27 in ready states, ~0 at reasoning start; ||dW||_2/||W||_2 = 0.04-0.19, far under the 5x limit. Non-math late states (story, code) get only a mild push since the gate is small there.
